problem:
Consider the vector field $F$ and the surface $S$ with unit normal vector $n,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨{z}^{2},\,x,\,y-{z}^{2}⟩\,,\,n(x,y,z)=\frac{1}{3}⟨2,\,-1,\,2⟩\,.
$$

If the flux of $F$ across $S$ with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S=\frac{1}{3}{∬}_{S}\boxed{}\,\text{d}S,
$$

what is the missing expression?

feedback.problem:
Consider the vector field $F$ and the surface $S$ with unit normal vector $n,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨xy,\,yz,\,xz⟩\,,\,n(x,y,z)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}⟨1,\,-1,\,2⟩\,.
$$

If the flux of $F$ across $S$ with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S=\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}{∬}_{S}\boxed{}\,\text{d}S,
$$

what is the missing expression?
feedback.worked_solution:
If $S$ is an oriented surface with unit normal vector $n,$ and $F$ is continuous vector field, then the flux of $F$ across $S$ measured with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S.
$$

Calculating the dot product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F\cdot n & =⟨xy,\,yz,\,xz⟩\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}⟨1,\,-1,\,2⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}⟨xy,\,yz,\,xz⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,-1,\,2⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}(xy-yz+2xz) \\  & =\frac{xy-yz+2xz}{\sqrt{6}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{S}\frac{xy-yz+2xz}{\sqrt{6}}\,\text{d}S \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}{∬}_{S}xy-yz+2xz\,\text{d}S.\end{aligned}
$$
